key_insight: CHORD introduces a universal generative pipeline that learns to synthesize and 'choreograph' 4D (3D + time) dynamics of deforming, interacting objects, replacing labor-intensive, category-specific rule-based workflows with a scalable learned approach.
problem_solved: Automatically generating diverse, physically plausible dynamic scenes (deformations, interactions, temporal behaviors) across object categories—avoiding manual, heuristic-heavy graphics pipelines that don't scale.
method: Object-centric 4D representation: decompose scenes into per-object spatiotemporal components to capture motion, deformation and interactions.
Learned generative pipeline: train a model to produce temporally coherent 3D sequences that model interactions and evolving geometry from data.
Controllable choreographing: provide conditioning or interfaces to steer synthesized behaviors for target interactions, timing, or scene-level goals.
impact: Makes realistic 4D scene synthesis scalable for graphics, simulation, data augmentation, and embodied AI, accelerating research and applications that need diverse, temporally coherent object dynamics.
visual_elements: High-level pipeline diagram: input scene/data → CHORD model → generated 4D sequence (time axis emphasized)
Before/after sequence grid: reference vs. synthesized temporal frames to show realism and coherence
Object-centric overlay: per-object trajectories, deformation heatmaps, and interaction links across time
Metrics & diversity chart: plots showing coverage, realism/physics plausibility, and controllability examples
paper_title: Choreographing a World of Dynamic Objects
paper_authors: Yanzhe Lyu, Chen Geng, Karthik Dharmarajan, Yunzhi Zhang, Hadi Alzayer
